result.topic_en: Corollaries on reading off primes of the forms (aa+1)/5, (aa+1)/13 and (aa+1)/10 from a table of divisors of aa+1, and a scholium warning that prime-power divisors of aa+1 must also be recorded.
result.transcription:
120 DE NVMERIS PRIMIS
Coroll. 4.
Simili modo omnes numeri $a$, quibus ſolus quinarius eſt adſcriptus, praebebunt omnes numeros primos formae $\frac{aa+1}{5}$, qui infra limitem 800000 continentur. Atque omnes numeri $a$, qui tantum diuiſorem 13 habebunt adſcriptum, praebebunt omnes numeros primos formae $\frac{aa+1}{13}$, infra limitem 307692 contentos.
Coroll. 5.
Qui autem numeri $a$ duos tantum diuiſores $\alpha$ et $\beta$ habebunt adſcriptos, id indicio erit, numeros $\frac{aa+1}{\alpha\beta}$ fore primos. Hinc quibus numeris $a$ tantum duo diuiſores 2 et 5 fuerint adſcripti, ex iis reperientur omnes numeri primi formae $\frac{aa+1}{10}$, qui quidem limitem 400000 non ſuperabunt.
Scholion 1.
Verum vt hae concluſiones ſint certae, probe notandum eſt, inter numeros $aa+1$, qui ſunt per numerum primum $4n+1$ diuiſibiles, etiam eiusmodi numeros contineri, qui ſint per quadratum $(4n+1)^2$, vel etiam per cubum $(4n+1)^3$, altioresue poteſtates $(4n+1)^4$, $(4n+1)^5$ etc. diuiſibiles. Quod quoties accidit, numero $a$ non ſolum diuiſor $4n+1$, ſed eius ſumma poteſtas, per quam numerus $aa+1$ fuerit diuiſibilis, adſcribi debebit, vt hoc modo omnes diuiſores primi numerorum $aa+1$ ipſa radice $a$ minores obtineantur. Si quidem diuiſor fuerit $=2$, nulla eius altior

items.quote: Simili modo omnes numeri $a$, quibus ſolus quinarius eſt adſcriptus, praebebunt omnes numeros primos formae $\frac{aa+1}{5}$, qui infra limitem 800000 continentur.
items.english: In a similar way all numbers a to which only the number 5 is attached will yield all prime numbers of the form (aa+1)/5 that lie below the limit 800000.

items.quote: Atque omnes numeri $a$, qui tantum diuiſorem 13 habebunt adſcriptum, praebebunt omnes numeros primos formae $\frac{aa+1}{13}$, infra limitem 307692 contentos.
items.english: And all numbers a which have only the divisor 13 attached will yield all prime numbers of the form (aa+1)/13 lying below the limit 307692.

items.quote: Qui autem numeri $a$ duos tantum diuiſores $\alpha$ et $\beta$ habebunt adſcriptos, id indicio erit, numeros $\frac{aa+1}{\alpha\beta}$ fore primos.
items.english: Those numbers a which have only two divisors α and β attached indicate that the numbers (aa+1)/(αβ) are prime.

items.quote: Hinc quibus numeris $a$ tantum duo diuiſores 2 et 5 fuerint adſcripti, ex iis reperientur omnes numeri primi formae $\frac{aa+1}{10}$, qui quidem limitem 400000 non ſuperabunt.
items.english: Hence from those numbers a to which only the two divisors 2 and 5 are attached, all prime numbers of the form (aa+1)/10 not exceeding the limit 400000 will be found.

items.quote: numero $a$ non ſolum diuiſor $4n+1$, ſed eius ſumma poteſtas, per quam numerus $aa+1$ fuerit diuiſibilis, adſcribi debebit, vt hoc modo omnes diuiſores primi numerorum $aa+1$ ipſa radice $a$ minores obtineantur.
items.english: Not only the divisor 4n+1 but its highest power dividing aa+1 must be attached to the number a, so that in this way all prime divisors of the numbers aa+1 smaller than the root a itself are obtained.
